rubric.why: Limiting friction is the greatest value of static friction.
rubric.description: Identifies limiting friction as the maximum static friction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as maximum static friction.

rubric.why: Limiting friction acts at the point just before motion starts.
rubric.description: States that it acts just before one surface starts moving over the other.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the just-before-motion condition.

modelAnswer: Limiting friction is the maximum value of static friction between two surfaces.
It acts just before one surface starts moving over the other.

rubric.why: The definition concerns what happens after a small displacement from equilibrium.
rubric.description: States that the body is slightly displaced from its position.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the body is slightly displaced.

rubric.why: A body in stable equilibrium tends to return to its original or equilibrium position.
rubric.description: States that the body tends to return to its original or equilibrium position.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it returns to its original or equilibrium position.

modelAnswer: A body is in stable equilibrium if, after being slightly displaced, it tends to return to its original position.
